title: Heaviest Stones Smash
statement:
Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones together and report what is left at the end.

Contract
- `stones` holds positive integer weights, in any order; it may be empty. Do not modify it.
- Each round, take the two heaviest stones. If their weights are equal, both disappear; otherwise only one stone remains, weighing the difference of the two.
- Continue until at most one stone remains. Return its weight, or `0` when none remain (including for an empty input).
- A single stone is never smashed.

Examples
- `[8, 3, 5, 1]`: `8` and `5` leave `3`; the two `3`s vanish; `1` remains, so the answer is `1`.
- `[6, 6]` cancel out completely, so the answer is `0`.
- `[20]` is never smashed, so the answer is `20`.
hints: Every round needs the two largest stones, and the leftover goes back into the pile.
Re-sorting after each smash works but repeats effort; use a structure that always hands you the current maximum.

Keep a max-heap: poll twice, push the difference when it is non-zero, and stop when one or zero stones remain (guard the empty case). Intended complexity: O(n log n) time because each of at most n rounds does O(log n) heap work, and O(n) space for the heap.
inputSyntax: Input: the stone weights separated by spaces or commas, for example: 8 3 5 1
